description: Matter that keeps itself in order: cells, heredity, evolution, energy, light, and death.

concepts.title: Life
concepts.summary: Matter that keeps itself in order by using energy and exporting disorder. A cell is a small, stubborn argument against entropy, and one that has been making its case for close to four billion years.

concepts.title: Origin of Life
concepts.summary: How chemistry became biology, roughly four billion years ago. We don't know the path, only that it happened once, early, on a young wet planet, and that it started small.

concepts.title: Cells
concepts.summary: The smallest unit that counts as alive: a boundary, a chemistry running inside it, and instructions for building more. Every animal, plant, and fungus is a society of them.

concepts.title: Mitochondria
concepts.summary: The power plants inside most cells, descended from bacteria that took up residence over a billion years ago. They still carry their own small piece of DNA, and they burn food to make the cell's energy currency.

concepts.title: Neurons
concepts.summary: Cells that pass signals by electricity and chemistry. A human brain holds tens of billions, each linked to thousands of others, and thought is what happens in the pattern of those links.

concepts.title: DNA
concepts.summary: A long molecule that stores instructions in a four-letter code, copied each time a cell divides. It's less a blueprint than a very old recipe book that keeps editing itself.

concepts.title: Genes
concepts.summary: Stretches of DNA that hold the instructions for making a particular protein or piece of RNA. Genes are switched on and off by the cell's circumstances, so the same code can build a neuron or a skin cell.

concepts.title: Mutation
concepts.summary: A copying error, a chemical change, a stray bit of radiation. Most do nothing, some do harm, and a very few help, which is the raw material evolution has always worked with.

concepts.title: RNA
concepts.summary: DNA's working copy and much more: it carries instructions to the cell's protein makers, builds them, and can even act as an enzyme. Some think it came before DNA.

concepts.title: Evolution
concepts.summary: Copies that aren't quite perfect, in a world that keeps some more than others. Given enough time, that plain loop produces eyes, wings, and the person reading this. Nobody plans it.

concepts.title: Natural Selection
concepts.summary: Individuals that happen to suit their surroundings leave more offspring, so their traits become more common. No foresight is needed, only variation, inheritance, and time.

concepts.title: Adaptation
concepts.summary: A trait that fits its owner to a way of life: a heron's legs, a cactus's spines. Each is a record of the problems that ancestors faced, written into the body.

concepts.title: Extinction
concepts.summary: Most species that have ever lived are gone. Some vanish slowly, others in mass events, and each clears room for something that couldn't have existed otherwise.

concepts.title: Metabolism
concepts.summary: The chemistry of staying organized: take in energy-rich food or light, spend some on building and repair, release the rest as heat. Life runs on a downhill flow and steers a little of it uphill.

concepts.title: ATP
concepts.summary: The small molecule every living thing uses as energy currency. Cells make and spend it constantly, and a person turns over roughly their own body weight of it in a day.

concepts.title: Photosynthesis
concepts.summary: Plants, algae, and some bacteria catch sunlight and use it to turn air and water into sugar and oxygen. Nearly every food chain starts here, and the oxygen we breathe is a by-product.

concepts.title: Death
concepts.summary: The end of a particular pattern, and the return of its material to the ground. Death is what keeps ecosystems turning over, and what gives memory, ritual, and love some of their weight.
